prompt: A researcher tests whether favorite music genre is associated with age group using a chi-square test of independence on a $3 \times 3$ table. The statistic is $\chi^2 = 11.3$ with df $= 4$. The critical value for $\alpha = 0.05$ with df $= 4$ is $9.488$ (so the $p$-value is less than $0.05$). What is the correct conclusion?

choices.label: Reject $H_0$; there is convincing evidence of an association between genre and age group.
Fail to reject $H_0$; there is not convincing evidence of an association.
Accept $H_0$; genre and age group are independent.
Reject $H_0$; age causes people to prefer certain genres.

hint: Chi-square tests reject when the statistic is LARGER than the critical value (big disagreement with $H_0$).

hints.text: Chi-square tests reject when the statistic is LARGER than the critical value (big disagreement with $H_0$).

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm up: with df $= 1$ the critical value is $3.841$; a statistic of $5.0$ exceeds it, so you reject. Same comparison here: is $11.3$ above $9.488$?
$11.3 > 9.488$, so $p < 0.05$: reject $H_0$. Then word the conclusion carefully — association, not cause.
A: reject $H_0$; convincing evidence of an association. (D overreaches: an observational survey cannot show causation.)

explanation: $H_0$: genre and age group are independent. $H_a$: they are associated.
Since $\chi^2 = 11.3$ exceeds the critical value $9.488$, the $p$-value is below $0.05$, so we reject $H_0$.
The correct wording is "convincing evidence of an association" (A). C uses "accept", which tests never do, and D claims causation from survey data.

alternativeExplanations.title: Check the df
steps: For a $3 \times 3$ table, df $= (3-1)(3-1) = 4$, matching the problem.
A chi-square with df $= 4$ has mean 4, so $11.3$ is nearly three times what chance alone would typically produce.
That is why it clears $9.488$ and we reject $H_0$: choice A.
